indicators.note: the letters for a and king put on the lady like clothing, so they go round her

parts.note: taken as written
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king
Nora is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman dressed up in a monarch's robe.
explanation.definitionFit: An anorak is a hooded waterproof jacket, a kind of outer garment.

clue.text: I fare badly in common sense. That's terrible!

indicators.note: the jumbled letters are placed inside the word for common sense

parts.note: nous is British informal for practical good sense

indicators.note: I FARE done badly means the letters are put in a poor, disordered state

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at how poorly they are getting on with ordinary good sense.
explanation.walkthrough: NOUS is everyday British slang for common sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Nefarious means wicked or criminal, a strong synonym for terrible in the moral sense.

parts.note: the rook is a black crow-like bird
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, 'that is'

explanation.surface: A bird is tagging along behind a novice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' just ushers in the definition: what follows is the beginner.
explanation.definitionFit: A rookie is a novice or new recruit, someone just starting out.

clue.text: Cat said to hold vigil following death of bird

indicators.note: said signals that the word for cat is spoken, giving its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: kitty is a pet name for a cat
a wake is a watch kept over a body before burial

explanation.surface: A cat is supposed to sit up keeping watch after a death, then the bird appears.
explanation.definitionFit: The kittiwake is a small gull of the North Atlantic, so it is a seabird.

parts.note: taken as written
tact is good judgement in dealing with people

explanation.surface: Someone of sound judgement, as a reference might put it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound in judgement' reads as one phrase; split it after 'Sound'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sound here means whole and undamaged, as in safe and sound.

clue.text: Two separate accounts of this man

wordplay.note: ISA, an individual savings account, then AC, the abbreviation for account

explanation.surface: A man of whom two different stories are told.
explanation.walkthrough: An ISA is a British tax-free savings account; AC is short for account. Put side by side they make a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac is a male first name, the son of Abraham in the Bible.

clue.text: Send up tip after short voyage

indicators.note: after places the tip's letters behind the shortened voyage
short means the word for voyage loses its last letter

parts.note: travel as a noun is a journey
a tip or pigsty is a filthy, messy place

explanation.surface: A traveller is told to pass on a tip after a brief trip.
explanation.walkthrough: A tip is British for a rubbish dump or a very untidy place, like a sty.
explanation.definitionFit: A travesty is a grotesque parody or mockery, which is what a send-up is.

definitions.meaning: usually means embarrassing, but a muscle spasm literally curls the toes
as a verb, to restrict or hamper

explanation.walkthrough: 'Toe-curling' suggests embarrassment; read literally, it is the spasm that makes toes curl, and 'tie' is the restricting sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A cramp is a painful muscle spasm, and to cramp is to restrict or hamper movement.

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
out can mean away from home, as in out of the country

explanation.surface: Someone barred from a harbour overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: To be left out is to be omitted or not included.

clue.text: Pet with paws may be grabbed around the waist

definitions.text: may be grabbed around the waist

parts.note: love is a term of endearment, like pet
to paw is to handle clumsily or touch

explanation.surface: A pet with paws gets picked up round its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Love handles are rolls of fat at the sides of the waist, which a partner might hold.

indicators.note: backward means the agents, mangle and a are all read in reverse order

parts.note: the CIA is the US intelligence agency
to mar is to spoil or damage
taken as written

explanation.surface: Slow-witted spies butcher a foreign tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backward' looks like an insult to the agents but it reverses the whole chain.
explanation.definitionFit: Aramaic is an ancient Semitic tongue, spoken in the time of Jesus.

clue.text: Body of headless poet found in the south of France

definitions.text: found in the south of France

parts.note: a carcass is a dead body

indicators.note: headless means the poet's name loses its first letter

parts.note: John Donne, the English metaphysical poet

explanation.surface: A beheaded poet's corpse turns up in southern France.
explanation.definitionFit: Carcassonne is a walled medieval city in the Languedoc region of southern France.

clue.text: I pace River Niger disguised as an American climber

indicators.note: disguised means the letters are dressed up in a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone walks along the Niger in disguise, posing as an American mountaineer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climber' suggests a mountaineer; here it is a climbing plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Virginia creeper is a North American vine that grows up walls, a climbing plant.

clue.text: Band loves to occupy the Palace of Westminster

indicators.note: the loves move into the parliament building, sitting inside it

parts.note: HP stands for Houses of Parliament, housed in the Palace of Westminster
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O; two loves give two Os

explanation.surface: A music group adores taking over Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' looks like a group of musicians but means a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoop is a circular band of metal or wood, as round a barrel.

indicators.note: off signals the letters are gone wrong and need rearranging

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The Arsenal kick-off and a veteran goalscorer.
explanation.walkthrough: Arsenal is a London football club, and the surface makes a scorer a goalscorer; here it is a writer of musical scores.
explanation.definitionFit: Palestrina was a sixteenth-century Italian composer, so an old writer of scores.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to try hard to achieve something
second meaning: the ship of Captain James Cook on his first voyage

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook's vessel' looks like a saucepan; it is Captain Cook's ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb for striving and also the name of the ship HMS Endeavour that Cook sailed to Australia.

clue.text: One politician stood up about six to ad-lib

parts.note: the Roman numeral I
MP is a Member of Parliament

indicators.note: about means the word for stood up goes around the six

parts.note: rose is the past tense of rise, to stand up
the Roman numeral VI

explanation.surface: A lone politician gets up around six o'clock to speak off the cuff.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'stood up' looks like a reversal; it is simply the word for having risen.
explanation.definitionFit: To improvise is to perform or speak without preparation, which is to ad-lib.

clue.text: Sailor and foreign soldier are rich

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman
und is German for and
a soldier ant is a caste of ant

explanation.surface: A sailor and a mercenary from abroad are wealthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Abundant means plentiful, and rich can mean plentifully supplied, as in rich in minerals.

clue.text: They may issue when hooters are struck

definitions.meaning: means flow out, as blood does
slang for noses, not car horns or factory sirens

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hooters' sounds like horns being sounded; it is slang for noses, and 'issue' means pour out.
explanation.definitionFit: Bleeding from the nose is a common result of being punched in the face.

clue.text: Resorts to overtake when back marker comes first

indicators.note: the last letter of the word for overtake is moved round to the front

parts.note: to pass is to go by another vehicle

explanation.surface: A racing driver turns to overtaking when the car at the back takes the lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back marker' is a motor-racing term for the slowest car; here it is the final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Spas are health resorts with mineral springs, places people go to relax.

indicators.note: the artist goes into the word with, sitting inside it

parts.note: taken as written
RA is a Royal Academician

explanation.surface: A painter walks in full of spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: A wraith is a ghost or apparition, a disembodied spirit.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: literally loosen tied-up hair
second meaning: the idiom for abandoning restraint

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally means unpinning one's hair and idiomatically means behaving freely and unwinding.

parts.note: ease is comfort, freedom from pain or worry

explanation.surface: It is the moment to soothe a child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kid' looks like a child; it is the verb meaning to joke with.
explanation.definitionFit: To kid someone is to tease them, joking at their expense.

indicators.note: producing means the letters are worked up into a new form

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A musical instrument causing a commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stir' is part of the letters, not the instruction to mix them.
explanation.definitionFit: The sitar is a long-necked Indian stringed instrument, plucked like a lute.

wordplay.note: a seal and an ant, two animals placed side by side

explanation.surface: Creatures working as a team can plug holes.
explanation.definitionFit: A sealant is a substance applied to make joints watertight or airtight.

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
read as ones, the plural of one: two Roman numeral Is

explanation.surface: Someone is made to drink their mixed drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe is loose: 'one's' must be read as 'ones', a pair of Is, since FORCE and a single I are a letter short.
explanation.definitionFit: An orifice is an opening, such as a mouth or vent.

parts.note: race in the sense of the human race, mankind
a tor is a rocky hilltop, as on Dartmoor in England

explanation.surface: A trainer sprints up to the summit.
explanation.definitionFit: A mentor is a trusted adviser or trainer, someone who coaches.

clue.text: Cobbler might do this for lady returning fish

indicators.note: returning means the word for the lady is read backwards

parts.note: her refers to a woman
the eel is a snakelike fish

explanation.surface: A shoemaker does a job for a woman bringing back seafood.
explanation.definitionFit: To reheel is to fit new heels to a shoe, a shoe-repairer's job.
